item.text: The Crime and Misconduct Commission held an inquiry following a referral about media concerns over encrypted police radio communications.
item.support: media organisations had expressed concern about the implementation of a Queensland Police Service (QPS) decision to adopt encrypted digital radio communication technology

item.text: The Commission examined how to balance media scrutiny and reporting with police safety, personal privacy and confidentiality.
item.support: The recommendations aim to reconcile and balance these competing interests

item.text: The Commission concluded that media access to police communications should protect operational safety and individual privacy.
item.support: the media should have access to police communications in a way that maintains the safety and security of police operations

item.text: The Commission recommended a secure feed from police dispatch records for authorised media outlets, with exclusions and delays for specified incidents.
item.support: secure electronic transfer of information about operational police activity via a direct data-feed

item.text: Its 14 recommendations also covered privacy safeguards, staffing, costs and continuing consultation between police and the media.
item.support: The Commission makes 14 recommendations to ensure efﬁcient, transparent and technically feasible information-sharing practices

item.quote: That the QPS take all necessary steps to safeguard the privacy of individuals by ensuring that information identifying a person be excluded from the dispatch data-feed.
That the establishment and ongoing costs associated with the delivery of the dispatch data-feed and media notes be met by the QPS.
